newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel army, PLO police clash in Bethlehem.
newsitem.headline: Israel army, PLO police clash in Bethlehem.

text.p: Israeli troops and Palestinian police exchanged gunfire on Wednesday by a Jewish holy site near the PLO-ruled West Bank town of Bethlehem, witnesses said.
Two Israelis, a soldier and a fireman, were wounded during the gun battle, the second such incident in the West Bank on Wednesday, rescue crews said.
Earlier an Israeli-Palestinian firefight erupted in Ramallah, north of Jerusalem, during clashes in which Israeli troops killed at least four Palestinians and wounded more than 300.

The clashes on Wednesday were part of widespread protests across the West Bank and Gaza Strip against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to open a tunnel in Jerusalem near Islam's third holiest shrine.
Witnesses said Bethlehem residents dived to the ground and ran for cover when the two forces -- formally partners in enforcing a 1993 Israeli-PLO peace deal -- shot at one another.
They said Israeli soldiers withdrew from the tomb area after the exchange of fire, while jubilant Palestinian police fired their weapons into the air.

The Bethlehem battle followed a fiery protest in which Palestinian demonstrators hurling stones and petrol bombs threatened to burn Rachel's Tomb, traditional grave of the wife of the biblical patriarch Jacob.
The Israeli army said Palestinian protesters fired on the troops, and that two soldiers were lightly injured by petrol bombs and stones.
Israeli troops then opened fire, wounding 12 Arabs, among them a Palestinian police colonel, hospital officials said.

They said Colonel Kifah Barakat, local commander of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's Force 17, was struck in the face by a rubber bullet while trying to mediate an end to the Bethlehem street battles.

The Tomb of Rachel has been a focus of political strife in recent months. Israelis have stirred Palestinian ire by blocking a lane of the main Bethlehem-Jerusalem road near the tomb to facilitate construction work at the site.
